key_insight: Omni123 enables a 3D-native generative foundation model by jointly leveraging abundant 2D data and scarce 3D assets, unifying text-to-2D and text-to-3D generation so 3D outputs remain geometrically consistent despite limited 3D supervision.
problem_solved: Bridges the data gap between plentiful 2D imagery and scarce high-quality 3D assets, avoiding indirect 2D-edit-then-lift pipelines that produce inconsistent 3D geometry.
method: Train a single generative backbone that ties text-conditioned 2D and 3D generation together so knowledge from large 2D corpora benefits 3D synthesis.
Introduce rendering-aware, view-consistent training objectives and shared latent representations to ensure geometric consistency across views and modalities.
Design data-efficient supervision and consistency losses that let the model learn 3D structure with limited explicit 3D examples while leveraging abundant 2D supervision.
impact: Enables reliable, geometry-consistent text-to-3D generation with far less 3D data and reduces reliance on slow optimization-based lifting — accelerating development of 3D content creation, simulation, and downstream 3D multimodal applications.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing unified training: text → shared backbone → 2D renderings and 3D outputs with consistency losses.
Before/after comparison: traditional 2D-edit-then-lift result vs Omni123’s native 3D output highlighting improved geometry.
Data composition chart: proportion of 2D vs 3D training data and how 2D data supports 3D learning.
Qualitative gallery of view-consistent 3D renders from single text prompts (multiple viewpoint thumbnails).
paper_title: Omni123: Exploring 3D Native Foundation Models with Limited 3D Data by Unifying Text to 2D and 3D Generation
paper_authors: Chongjie Ye, Cheng Cao, Chuanyu Pan, Yiming Hao, Yihao Zhi
